About

Clarity is the product.

I'm maleekskies. I build full stack web apps, automate business workflows with AI, and write about technology. If your project needs a developer who also tests and explains, that's the work I do best; I build web apps for clients around the world, and I've shipped more than 15 of them as websites and PWAs. Over time I started automating the work that surrounds them: replies, alerts, follow-ups, and lead tracking.

I build my automations with n8n, and I can run them on your own infrastructure with locally hosted AI for more privacy and lower running costs, or integrate with paid services like OpenAI/Claude if you prefer. You get to choose what fits your business best.

I'm also a software tester and I write threads, articles, and research for Web3 and AI projects.

AI Automation

Automations that keep running without me.

AI Automation · Customer Support · Lead Management

MK: Automated Customer Support & Lead Follow-Up System

A complete support and follow-up workflow built in n8n. When a customer submits an inquiry, the system checks it, writes a short reply with a locally hosted AI model, emails it through Gmail, alerts the business on Telegram, and follows up automatically if the customer doesn't respond.

  1. Google FormInquiry submitted
  2. Google SheetsLead saved
  3. n8nValidate and structure
  4. OllamaDrafts the reply
  5. Gmail + TelegramReply sent, team alerted
  6. Wait and checkDid they reply?
  7. Follow-upEmail and sheet update
Workflow logicLocal AI

The problem

Handling new inquiries by hand means checking forms, writing replies, telling the team, and remembering to follow up. Each step is small, but together they cost time, and leads get missed.

The solution

One workflow handles the whole path, from the form to the follow-up. n8n runs self-hosted in Docker and the AI model runs locally through Ollama, so no paid AI APIs are involved.

How it works

  1. Capture. A customer submits a Google Form with their name, email, phone number, business, service needed, budget, and project description. The response lands in Google Sheets, which acts as the lead database and starts the workflow.
  2. Validate. n8n checks that the required details are there, especially the email address, and cleans the lead into consistent fields.
  3. Reply. A locally hosted Ollama model reads the inquiry and writes a short, professional response that sticks to what the customer actually said. Gmail sends it.
  4. Alert. At the same moment, Telegram notifies the business with the lead's details. Both paths rejoin before the follow-up logic starts.
  5. Wait and check. The workflow waits a set period, then checks Gmail for a reply from the customer.
  6. Follow up. If there's no reply, Gmail sends a follow-up and the lead's record in Google Sheets is updated with the follow-up status.

What it handles

One connected workflow

Google Forms, Google Sheets, Gmail, Telegram, and Ollama work together as a single process, from first inquiry to follow-up.

Local AI

The reply is written by a model running locally through Ollama, with n8n self-hosted in Docker and no paid AI APIs.

Follow-ups that need no reminders

The workflow checks whether the customer replied and only follows up if they haven't, then updates the lead's status.

Business value

  • New leads are captured immediately, and customers get a fast reply.
  • The team is notified the moment an inquiry arrives.
  • Unanswered leads are followed up automatically.
  • Lead status stays organized in the CRM.
  • Inquiries are far less likely to be forgotten.

Built with

Real Estate Operations & Sales Automation

Skies Realty: Automated AI Lead Management & CRM Pipeline

When a property inquiry comes in, the system scores it, summarizes the buyer's notes with a locally hosted AI model, logs it to a CRM sheet, and alerts the sales team on Telegram within moments. Scoring and budget logic run in plain code, and no customer data is sent to a third-party AI service.

  1. Google FormInquiry submitted
  2. n8nWebhook & JSON mapping
  3. Priority scoreDeterministic code
  4. OllamaOne-line intent summary
  5. Google SheetsCRM row, 11 fields
  6. TelegramPriority alert
Code decides the numbersLocal AI only reads the language

The problem

In real estate, a delayed response directly costs conversions. Manual lead logging is slow and inconsistent, and the unstructured notes buyers write are hard for sales reps to scan quickly.

Handing those notes to a cloud AI would fix the reading problem, but it would also send client names, phone numbers, and budgets to a third party and add a per-token bill.

The solution

An n8n workflow takes each inquiry from form submission to a scored, logged lead and a Telegram alert, with nobody in the loop.

Code decides everything numerical, and a local LLM only reads and summarizes the text. Because the model runs locally, customer data is never sent to a third-party AI service, and there are no per-token fees.

How it works

  1. Capture. A prospect submits the Google Form, which triggers the n8n workflow.
  2. Normalize. Dynamic JSON expressions map the payload into one clean, consistent object.
  3. Score. A deterministic code node computes the lead's priority score from the structured fields.
  4. Summarize. The free-text "Tell us what you're looking for" field goes to the local Ollama model, which returns a single-sentence summary of intent.
  5. Log. The lead is written to the Google Sheets CRM with every value mapped to an exact header: Timestamp, Full Name, Email Address, Phone Number, Property Type, Preferred Location, Purpose, Budget Range, Preferred Move-in Date, the buyer's own words, and the AI Summary.
  6. Alert. The Telegram Bot API pushes a priority-routed alert to the sales team, summary and score included.
  7. Notify. Email notifications go out through Gmail SMTP.

Engineering highlights

Hybrid by design

Scoring and budget logic live in strict code nodes, so the same lead always gets the same score. The LLM never touches a number.

Local AI inference

The model runs locally, so customer details are never sent to a third-party AI vendor.

No per-token costs

Self-hosted summarization keeps the AI bill flat as lead volume grows.

Schema-exact mapping

Dynamic JSON mapping matches all 11 CRM headers, so every row lands clean.

Batching-safe execution

Fallback array-referencing logic prevents mismatched data when a run handles multiple items.

Quick to read

A one-sentence summary and a priority alert let a rep understand a lead at a glance.

Impact

  • A lead's first alert no longer depends on someone being at a desk.
  • Every lead lands in the CRM in the same structure, with a score attached.
  • Reps read one sentence instead of a paragraph of raw notes.
  • No per-token AI fees, and customer data is never sent to a third-party AI service.

Built with

Case study

Huntboard

A job search platform that finds roles, scores them against your CV, and builds the application for you.

Full Stack · AI-Powered Job Search

Huntboard: Scan, Score and Apply From One Place

Huntboard scans multiple job boards, scores each role against a user's CV with a hybrid keyword and LLM engine, and generates a tailored CV and cover letter per role through its kit system.

  1. Job boardsRoles scanned
  2. Keyword engineFast first pass
  3. LLM (Groq)Deeper match check
  4. InboxScored roles
  5. KitCV and cover letter
Keywords narrow it downThe LLM judges the fit

The problem

Searching for a job means checking several boards, reading long descriptions, and guessing which roles actually fit. Then each application needs its own tailored CV and cover letter.

The solution

One workspace that gathers roles, ranks them against the user's CV and preferences, and explains each match. For the roles worth pursuing, the kit system drafts the CV and cover letter.

How it works

  1. Scan. Roles are collected from multiple job boards into one list.
  2. Score. A hybrid engine combines keyword matching with an LLM, so the score reflects both exact skills and overall fit.
  3. Review. The inbox shows every role scored against the CV and preferences. Each job opens with a match breakdown.
  4. Prepare. The kit shows why a role matches and which gaps to address, then generates a tailored CV and cover letter for that role.

Engineering highlights

Hybrid scoring

Keywords give a fast first pass and the LLM adds judgement, so results are not just word counts.

Explained matches

Each score comes with a breakdown and a list of gaps, so the user knows what to fix.

Per-role kits

Every application gets its own CV and cover letter instead of one generic copy.

Built with

Case study

ChessHatch

A chess platform that teaches from the first move and grows with the player.

Full Stack · Chess Learning Platform

ChessHatch: Learn, Practise and Play in One Place

ChessHatch is a learning-first chess platform. Lessons start from zero and build to 50 tactics lessons, a rule-based live coach explains moves, multiplayer is real time with Glicko-2 ratings, and Stockfish runs offline with nine bot levels that unlock as you win.

  1. LessonsFrom zero
  2. Tactics10 series, 50 lessons
  3. Live coachRule-based hints
  4. Bots9 levels, Stockfish
  5. MultiplayerGlicko-2 ratings
Coach rules run in code

The problem

Many chess sites assume you already know the game. Beginners are dropped into matches or a wall of puzzles with no clear path from the basics to real tactics.

The solution

A structured path: beginner lessons, then tactics in ten series, then bots and live opponents. The coach explains what is happening on the board, so practice teaches something.

How it works

  1. Learn. Beginner lessons start from zero and build step by step.
  2. Train. Intermediate tactics are grouped into 10 series with 50 lessons in total.
  3. Get coached. A rule-based live coach comments on the position as you play.
  4. Play. Face one of nine Stockfish bot levels, which unlock as you win. Bot play works offline.
  5. Compete. Real-time multiplayer uses Glicko-2 ratings to match and rank players.

Engineering highlights

Offline computer play

Stockfish.js runs in the browser, so bot games work without a connection.

Real-time multiplayer

Live games with Glicko-2 ratings, which handle new and returning players more fairly than simple Elo.

Unlockable progression

Bot levels open as you win, which gives players a reason to keep going.

Built with
